about.title: About Paxl
about.subtitle: A visual landing page editor built as a personal project.
about.missionBody: Paxl is a block-based landing page editor. It is a complete project from end to end: an editor with a lot of state in the browser, its own API, real-time collaboration and AI generation that returns valid blocks instead of free text.
about.authorBody: David Palmero, web developer. The code is public and the architecture decisions are documented in the repository.
about.principle1Body: Every block has defined fields. It gives less freedom than a blank canvas, but the page doesn't fall apart and AI can generate blocks that fit.
about.principle2Body: Colors, fonts and spacing are chosen once for the whole page and blocks inherit them. Switching palettes changes the whole page at once.
about.principle3Body: Changes reach the server a few seconds after you make them. No need to remember to save.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: Paxl is the demo of a personal project, not a commercial service. This page explains, plainly, what data it handles, what for, for how long, who it is shared with and what you can do about it. It is not intended for children under 14. I recommend not using real personal data: a test name and email are enough.
privacy.section1Body: The data controller is David Palmero Jara. For anything about privacy (exercising your rights, questions, notices) write to davidpalmerojara@gmail.com.
privacy.section2Title: What data is stored, what for and on what legal basis
privacy.section2Body:
• Your account: username, email and password (stored as a hash); if you sign in with Google, also your Google identifier, name and picture. They let you sign in and use the app. Legal basis: performing the service you ask for (GDPR art. 6(1)(b)).
• Your content: the pages you create, their versions, the images you upload and the messages your forms receive. They let me give you the editor and show your pages. Same legal basis.
• Guest session: a temporary account with no email, created when you try the app without signing up. Same purpose and legal basis.
• Emails: your address is used to send you the magic link you ask for and, if someone shares a page with you, the matching notice. Legal basis: performing the service you ask for (the link) and legitimate interest in notifying whoever is invited to collaborate (the notice).
• Visits to published pages: minimal, cookieless analytics (next section). Legal basis: legitimate interest (art. 6(1)(f)) in knowing whether pages are visited, with as little data as possible.
• Messages from the contact form of a published page: the name, email and message written by whoever visits it, so the page author can read them. The IP is not stored. Legal basis: your request when you send it. The page author decides what to do with them.
• Security: the IP address is used in memory to limit abuse (sign-in attempts, sign-ups, sends) and is not stored in the database; the hosting providers may record it in their logs (section "Who it is shared with"). Legal basis: legitimate interest in the security of the service.
privacy.section3Body: Analytics on published pages uses no cookies and stores nothing on the visitor's device. It records the page path (without URL parameters), the origin of the referring site, UTM tags, screen size, the block clicked and where its links point, and an anonymous identifier the server computes from the IP and browser with a key that changes every day. The IP and browser are not stored, and the identifier cannot recognise a person across different days. Events are deleted after 90 days.
privacy.section4Body:
• Account and content: until you delete your account; its pages, versions, images and messages are deleted with it. Each page keeps at most 20 versions.
• Guest accounts and everything in them: 24 hours; a daily automatic cleanup deletes them.
• Visit statistics: 90 days.
• Record of sent emails: for each email, a hash of the address (not the address), its type and the date are kept, only to count the daily sending limits; it is deleted after 30 days.
• Magic links: they expire after 15 minutes and are deleted after 24 hours.
• Session: access lasts 1 hour and the session renews for up to 7 days; signing out invalidates it.
• Backups: the database provider keeps a history of a few hours and occasional copies of the database may exist; what you delete stops being available at once, but may take a limited time to disappear from those copies.
privacy.section5Body: Two cookies keep you signed in (bp_access and bp_refresh), and they exist only if you sign in or start a guest session. Another cookie, paxl-locale, remembers the language only when you change it with the switcher; if you never touch it, the app uses your browser's language and stores nothing. The browser's local storage keeps your light or dark theme preference (when you change it) and a backup of the page you are editing, so a network failure does not lose your changes. Published pages set no cookies and store nothing on the device of whoever visits them.
privacy.section6Body:
These providers are used to run Paxl. They process data on my behalf and only to provide their service:
• Vercel (USA): hosts the website and forwards requests to the API; it sees the IP addresses of whoever visits Paxl and may record them in its logs.
• Render (USA, server in Frankfurt): runs the Paxl server; its logs may include IP addresses and the paths requested.
• Neon (USA, database in Frankfurt): stores all the data from the sections above, images included.
• Brevo (France): sends the emails (magic link and sharing notices); it receives the recipient's address and the text of the message.
• Google (USA): only if you choose "Continue with Google"; Google knows you signed in here. Its script is loaded only on the sign-in and sign-up screens, and only if the server has that sign-in configured: published pages and the rest of the app never contact Google.
• GitHub (USA): hosts the source code and runs the daily automatic cleanup of the database; it receives no user data.
Providers based in the USA may process data outside the European Economic Area with safeguards such as standard contractual clauses or the EU-US Data Privacy Framework.
privacy.section7Body: In the demo, AI generation sends nothing to any provider: it serves pages and block variants that were saved beforehand, and it says so on screen. Only if you enter your own Google (Gemini) or Anthropic key are your instruction and the block content sent to that provider for that request; the key is only used for it and is not stored. Payments are turned off in the demo: no payment data is asked for or stored; if they are turned on, they go through Stripe in test mode and nothing is charged.
privacy.section8Body: Data is not sold or used for advertising, no profiles are built and no automated decisions are made about you, and there are no third-party cookies or analytics. It is only used to make the app work.
privacy.section9Body: You have the right to access your data, correct it, erase it, restrict its processing, object to it and receive it in a usable format (portability). You can delete your account yourself from Settings; for anything else, write to davidpalmerojara@gmail.com and I will answer within one month at most. If you think your data is not being handled properly, you can lodge a complaint with the Spanish Data Protection Agency (aepd.es).
privacy.section10Body: You can delete your account yourself from Settings, under Delete account (it asks for your password or for you to type your username). Your account, your pages and their versions, the messages received through forms, the analytics and the images you uploaded are permanently deleted. If you have an active paid subscription, it has to be cancelled first. Guest accounts delete themselves after 24 hours. If something goes wrong, write to davidpalmerojara@gmail.com.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.intro: Short terms for using the Paxl demo. By using it, you accept them.
terms.section1Body: Paxl is a personal project by David Palmero Jara (davidpalmerojara@gmail.com), offered as is and free of charge. It may change, break or go offline without notice, and data may be lost. Don't use it for anything important. Guest accounts are deleted after 24 hours, and there are storage and usage limits per account.
terms.section2Body: Don't publish illegal or misleading content (for example, pages that impersonate a person or a company or ask for passwords or payment details) or content that infringes other people's rights, and don't try to overload or attack the service. Pages or accounts that do may be removed without notice. Accounts without a verified email publish with restrictions: no custom HTML, hidden from search engines and with a contact form that does not send.
terms.section3Title: Published content and how to report it
terms.section3Body: Whoever publishes a page is responsible for its content, and whoever fills in a page's contact form sends their data to that page's author. If you find illegal, fraudulent or rights-infringing content on a page published with Paxl, write to davidpalmerojara@gmail.com with the address of the page and I will remove whatever is appropriate.
terms.section4Body: Payments are turned off in this demo and, meanwhile, every account has the Pro features. If they are turned on, they run in Stripe's test mode: nothing is charged and no real card is needed.
terms.section5Body: What you create in Paxl is yours: it is only used to show your pages and to make the editor work, and you give me permission to host and show it while your account exists. Paxl's code can be read on GitHub for review, but it may not be copied, modified or reused without written permission (all rights reserved, see the LICENSE file).
terms.section6Body: Paxl is offered without warranties of any kind and, as far as the law allows, the author is not liable for data loss or for damage arising from its use. These terms are governed by Spanish law. How your personal data is handled is explained on the Privacy page.

changelog.title: Changelog
changelog.subtitle: What has changed in Paxl, taken from the repository history.
changelog.entry1Body: Images are stored in the database, re-encoded and with quotas. Email goes out through the Brevo API with daily caps. While payments are off, every account has the Pro features, and accounts that have not verified their email publish like guests. Storage limits, analytics retention and free deployment on Vercel, Render and Neon.
changelog.entry2Body: Three rounds of testing across the editor, mobile, accessibility and security: AA contrast on published pages, a touch editor for tablets, sessions and invite links that can be closed, strict image URLs and access limits for everyone. The most important bugs are told in the repository.
changelog.entry3Body: Editing together with other people: presence, per-block locks, cursors, invite links and a three-way merge. A 24-hour guest mode, free demo AI, cookieless analytics, a contact form and server-rendered published pages.
changelog.entry4Body: Django backend with accounts, pages, versions, analytics, billing and real-time collaboration. Pages dashboard, publishing, server autosave and a mobile editor.
changelog.entry5Body: Visual editor with blocks, a properties inspector, drag and drop, undo and redo. Pages were saved in the browser.

collab.revokedTitle: You no longer have access to this page
collab.revokedBody: The owner stopped sharing it with you. The page is now read-only: anything not saved yet will not be saved.
collab.lockRejectedOwnTab: You are editing it in another tab
collab.deletedBody: The owner deleted it. It can no longer be edited and no changes will be saved.

join.title: Join a page
join.invalidBody: It may have expired or been used by too many people. Ask whoever sent it for a new one.
join.throttledBody: Many sessions were started from this connection. Wait a while and open the link again.
join.capacityBody: There are too many guest sessions open. Please try again later.
join.errorBody: Something went wrong. Open the link again in a moment.

apiErrors.session: Your session has expired. Please log in again.
apiErrors.forbidden: You don't have permission to do this.
apiErrors.notOwner: Only the page owner can do this.
apiErrors.notFound: The page no longer exists or you no longer have access to it.
apiErrors.conflict: Someone changed the page at the same time.
apiErrors.throttled: Too many requests in a row. Wait a moment.

saveStatus.offline: Offline. Your changes are kept in this browser and will be sent as soon as you're back online.
saveStatus.failedRetrying: Your changes couldn't be saved. {reason} We'll try again shortly.
saveStatus.rejectedShort: {count, plural, one {# field not saved} other {# fields not saved}}
saveStatus.rejected: Couldn't save “{field}”{others, plural, =0 {} one { (and # more field)} other { (and # more fields)}}: {message} Everything else is still being saved.
saveStatus.versionNeedsSave: The version can't be saved until your changes are.
saveStatus.aiNeedsSave: AI works on the saved page and your latest changes couldn't be saved. Try again once they are.
saveStatus.recovered: We recovered changes from this browser that hadn't been saved. Press {undo} to undo.
saveStatus.leaveMessage: Your latest changes couldn't be saved. If you leave, they stay in this browser and come back when you open the page again.

publishing.unpublishMessage: It will no longer be visible at its public address. The draft stays as it is and you can publish it again whenever you like.
